summary:
**Sonara Earth** is an interactive 3D Earth visualization platform that transforms complex climate and geophysical data into visual and audio experiences. Built using CesiumJS, JavaScript, Python, and the Web Audio API, it allows users to explore historical global temperature changes (1850–2025), rainfall, wind patterns, ocean currents, tides, and tectonic plate boundaries on a realistic 3D globe.

Its unique feature is a Binaural Fire Sonification Engine, which converts temperature data into realistic fire-like sounds and musical tones. Users can select two locations on Earth and compare their temperatures through separate left and right headphone channels, making climate differences easier to perceive.

By combining scientific visualization with sound, Thermophone Earth makes complex Earth science data more interactive, accessible, and engaging. It helps users explore environmental changes, understand regional climate differences, and experience our planet's changing systems in an entirely new way.
details:
Thermophone Earth – Project Details

1. Project Overview

Thermophone Earth is an interactive 3D planetary visualization platform designed to help people explore, understand, and experience Earth's changing environmental and geophysical systems. It combines realistic satellite-based Earth visualization, historical scientific datasets, interactive geographical analysis, and real-time audio generation to transform complex scientific information into an engaging visual and auditory experience.

The platform provides a realistic 3D globe similar to Google Earth, allowing users to explore our planet and activate different scientific layers to understand environmental patterns and changes over time.

2. How Does the Project Work?

Thermophone Earth integrates multiple Earth science datasets into an interactive 3D globe. Users can explore different environmental parameters through selectable visualization layers.

The major features include:

  • Global Temperature Visualization: Displays historical global temperature anomalies from 1850 to 2025 using NOAA Global Surface Temperature data. Users can explore temperature changes across different years and months.
  • Rainfall Visualization: Displays global precipitation patterns using NASA GPM and GPCP-related datasets, helping users understand variations in rainfall distribution.
  • Wind Visualization: Uses atmospheric wind vector data from NOAA GFS and ECMWF ERA5 to generate animated wind streamlines, showing wind direction and movement.
  • Ocean Current Visualization: Integrates NASA OSCAR and NOAA OISST datasets to display ocean current movements and sea surface temperature patterns.
  • Ocean Tide Visualization: Uses global tidal models to visualize tidal ranges and calculate tidal variations through harmonic models.
  • Tectonic Plate Visualization: Displays global tectonic plate boundaries, identifying convergent, divergent, and transform boundaries.

Users can activate, deactivate, and adjust the opacity of different scientific layers to explore environmental conditions independently or together.

3. Innovative Binaural Fire Sonification Engine

One of the most creative features of Thermophone Earth is its Binaural Fire Sonification Engine.

Instead of presenting temperature differences only through numerical values and color-coded maps, our project converts temperature information into realistic fire-like sounds and musical tones using the Web Audio API.

The system procedurally generates three main acoustic components:

  • Convective thermal roar, representing the movement of hot air.
  • Wood crackles and popping embers, representing temperature-dependent fire activity.
  • Oxygen hiss, representing the sound of air during combustion.

As temperature changes, the characteristics of the generated sound, including frequency, intensity, and crackling behavior, also change.

Users can select two geographical locations, Pin A and Pin B, on the globe. The application calculates the geographical distance between them and compares their temperature values.

Using binaural audio, the temperature of Pin A is played through the left headphone channel, while Pin B is played through the right channel. This allows users to hear and compare temperature differences through sound.

The system also includes three audio modes: Fire Only, Notes Only, and Blend Mode. It can map temperature values to musical notes and identify musical intervals between the selected locations.

4. Technologies and Tools Used

We developed the project using modern web technologies and scientific data-processing tools.

  • CesiumJS: Used to create the interactive 3D Earth globe, render geographical data layers, manage camera movement, place geographical markers, and visualize geodesic paths.
  • JavaScript (ES6+): Handles application logic, user interactions, data coordination, and communication between different modules.
  • Web Audio API: Generates procedural fire sounds, musical tones, and binaural stereo audio for comparing temperatures.
  • Python: Used for scientific data preprocessing and conversion.
  • xarray and netCDF4: Used to process multidimensional scientific NetCDF datasets and convert them into optimized JSON grids.
  • HTML5 and CSS3: Used to build the user interface, interactive controls, floating panels, and visual components.
  • OpenStreetMap Nominatim: Supports geographical search and location identification.
  • Python HTTP Server: Used to serve the application locally during development.

5. Scientific Data Processing

Our project integrates Earth observation and geophysical datasets from organizations such as NASA, NOAA, ECMWF, and other scientific research institutions.

Large scientific NetCDF datasets are processed using Python, xarray, and netCDF4. The data is regridded into compact JSON arrays to make it easier for the browser to load and visualize scientific information.

The processed data is then integrated into the application, where CesiumJS displays the information as geographical overlays and the audio engine uses temperature values to generate corresponding sounds.

This approach makes complex scientific datasets easier to explore through an interactive web application.

6. What Makes Our Project Creative and Unique?

The main innovation of Thermophone Earth is its combination of scientific visualization and sound-based data interpretation.

Traditional Earth visualization platforms mainly communicate environmental information through maps, colors, graphs, and numerical values. Thermophone Earth introduces another way of understanding this information by translating temperature variations into natural fire-like sounds and musical tones.

The binaural comparison feature allows users to experience differences between two geographical locations through their headphones, creating an additional sensory dimension to climate data exploration.

The integration of multiple environmental layers into a single interactive 3D planetary platform also allows users to explore the relationships between different Earth systems.

7. Benefits and Intended Impact

Thermophone Earth aims to make Earth science information more accessible, understandable, and engaging.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Helping students and educators understand global climate patterns through interactive visualization.
  • Making historical temperature changes easier to explore and compare.
  • Improving public awareness of climate change and environmental variations.
  • Helping users explore atmospheric and oceanic systems through geographical visualization.
  • Introducing sound-based scientific data interpretation as an alternative to conventional visual representations.
  • Providing an interactive platform for exploring Earth's interconnected environmental systems.

By combining visualization, geographical analysis, and audio sonification, the project creates a new way to experience and understand our planet.

8. Design and Development Considerations

During development, we focused on creating a modular, efficient, and user-friendly application.

We used a centralized state management system to coordinate the different components and ensure that changes in the interface are reflected consistently across the globe, scientific layers, and audio engine.

A layer registry system manages the loading, activation, removal, and opacity of scientific layers. Scientific datasets are loaded when required to avoid unnecessary resource usage.

We also considered browser performance, efficient data processing, geographical accuracy using the WGS84 ellipsoid, and an intuitive interface that makes complex scientific information easier to explore.

Overall, Thermophone Earth transforms Earth science data into an interactive experience where users can not only see our planet's changing environmental conditions but also hear and compare them.
